title: Sit with the lynching memorial in Montgomery
place: National Memorial for Peace and Justice
description: Eight hundred hanging steel columns, one for each county where a lynching took place, each carrying names. Allow the whole afternoon and expect it to be hard.

title: Swim off the quartz sand at Gulf State Park
description: Sand ground down from Appalachian quartz, so it stays cool underfoot in August, with 45km of trail behind the dunes.

title: Stand under a Saturn V at the Rocket Center
description: The largest collection of rockets anywhere, including a Saturn V lying on its side that is longer than a football pitch.

title: Bathe in a Hot Springs bathhouse
description: Forty-seven springs at 62 degrees plumbed into Edwardian bathhouses in the middle of town. The Buckstaff still runs the old way.

title: Paddle the Buffalo National River
description: The first national river in the country, protected undammed in 1972, beneath limestone bluffs 150 metres above the water.

title: Paddle into the Okefenokee at dawn
description: A peat bog the size of a county holding perhaps ten thousand alligators, with water stained black by tannin and overnight platforms out in it.

title: Walk the Atlanta BeltLine Eastside Trail
description: A disused rail loop being turned into 35km of park and path around the city. The Eastside stretch is finished, free and always busy.

title: Walk out onto the Ledge at Skydeck
description: Glass boxes cantilevered 412 metres up with nothing under your feet but Wacker Drive.

title: Follow what is left of Route 66 through Illinois
description: The original alignment still runs in pieces beside the interstate, through diners and neon that survived being bypassed in 1977.

title: Climb or walk the arches of Red River Gorge
description: More than a hundred natural sandstone arches, and some of the best sport climbing in the country on the same rock.

title: Stand at the Churchill Downs finish line
description: The Derby has run on the first Saturday in May since 1875. Outside race week the track and museum are quiet and cheap.

title: See the mill buildings full of art at MASS MoCA
description: Twenty-six former factory buildings in North Adams, holding art too big for a normal gallery, including a Sol LeWitt wall drawing retrospective on for decades.

title: Watch whales on Stellwagen Bank
description: A submerged sandbank that concentrates sand lance, and with them humpbacks that feed by blowing nets of bubbles.

title: Drive the North Shore to Grand Marais
description: A hundred and fifty miles along the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, with eight state parks and a waterfall in most.

title: Skate the Chain of Lakes when it freezes
description: The city ploughs rinks straight onto the lake ice and leaves them free and open. Locals treat it as a commute, not an outing.

title: Follow the Blues Trail through the Delta
description: Markers at the places the music actually came from, and juke joints in Clarksdale that still put a band on midweek.

title: Walk the siege lines at Vicksburg
description: Forty-seven days of siege ended on 4 July 1863 and split the Confederacy in two. The park road runs along both armies' earthworks.

title: Float the Current River
description: Spring-fed and cold enough to be a shock in August, through the first river system in the country protected as a national park unit.

title: Eat Kansas City barbecue at a burnt-ends counter
description: Burnt ends began as offcuts given away at the end of the brisket. Now people queue for them, which the original butchers would find funny.

title: Soak outdoors at Chico Hot Springs
description: An 1900 hot spring resort in Paradise Valley, open all year, and at its best when it is snowing on you.

title: Walk the Little Bighorn battlefield
description: White markers where the Seventh Cavalry fell, and since 2003 a memorial to the Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho who beat them.

title: Walk the Flume Gorge boardwalk
description: A 240-metre granite cleft with walls 27 metres high, walked on a boardwalk bolted into the rock since 1808.

title: Walk colonial Portsmouth and eat on the waterfront
description: One of the oldest towns in the country, small enough to cross in twenty minutes, with a working harbour still at the end of the street.

title: Watch synchronous fireflies at Elkmont
description: One of very few places on earth where fireflies flash in unison, for about two weeks in June. Access is by lottery.

title: See the Biltmore Estate and its grounds
description: The largest privately owned house in the United States at 16,000 square metres, with grounds laid out by the man who designed Central Park.

title: Stargaze in one of the darkest skies in the lower 48
description: Western North Dakota has almost no light domes at all. On a clear moonless night the Milky Way casts a shadow.

title: See the geographic centre of North America marker
description: A stone obelisk on a claim first made in 1931 by a rough calculation, disputed ever since, and cheerfully signposted anyway.

title: Walk to Old Man's Cave
description: A blackhand sandstone gorge of recess caves and waterfalls, cut into the one corner of Ohio the glaciers missed. Free.

title: See where the Wright brothers actually worked
description: The bicycle shop and the print works, not the beach at Kitty Hawk. Free, and the aircraft are at the Air Force museum up the road.

title: Watch WaterFire burn on the rivers
description: Eighty braziers lit on the water at sunset on scheduled nights and tended by crews in black boats. Free to watch.

title: Cycle around Block Island
description: Ten square miles reached by ferry, with 45 per cent of it under conservation and bluffs 45 metres above the Atlantic.

title: Walk the boardwalk under the champion trees
description: The largest old-growth bottomland hardwood forest left in the country, with some of the tallest trees in eastern North America. Free.

title: Hear Gullah Geechee history in the Lowcountry
description: The Penn Center was one of the first schools for freed people in the South, and the language and cooking of the sea islands are still their own.

title: Walk or ski the Stowe Recreation Path
description: Eight kilometres of paved path along the West Branch, free, and groomed for cross-country skiing once the snow comes.

title: Watch the sun set over Lake Champlain
description: The Adirondacks on the far shore turn the whole lake orange. The bike path along the waterfront runs out onto a causeway into the lake.

title: Visit the telescope in the National Radio Quiet Zone
description: Thirty-three thousand square kilometres where mobile phones and wifi are restricted by law, so a 100-metre dish can listen across the galaxy.

title: Raft the Gauley during the autumn dam releases
description: Twenty-two weekend days a year when the Summersville dam releases, turning the river into some of the hardest commercially run water in the country.

title: Eat at a Door County fish boil
description: Whitefish and potatoes boiled over an open fire, finished by throwing kerosene on the flames so the oil boils over the rim.

title: Eat cheese curds that squeak at the Dane County market
description: The largest producer-only farmers' market in the country, around the Capitol square. If the curds do not squeak they are not fresh.

title: Scramble to the summit of Old Rag
description: A granite scramble with real hand-over-hand sections near the top. Day-use tickets are capped and must be booked ahead.

title: Walk colonial Williamsburg out of season
description: The largest living history museum in the country. In winter the crowds go and the interpreters have time to talk properly.

title: Cycle the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
description: Eighteen kilometres from downtown Anchorage along the Cook Inlet mudflats, with belugas offshore and the occasional moose on the path. Free.

title: Walk to the face of the Mendenhall Glacier
description: A glacier reachable on a city bus, with a free lakeside trail to a waterfall beside the ice. The visitor centre charges; the trail does not.

title: Walk the Wynwood murals
description: A warehouse district turned open-air gallery from 2009. The surrounding streets are free; only the walled courtyard is ticketed.

title: Drive Loop Road through Big Cypress at dusk
description: Forty kilometres of gravel through cypress swamp with alligators on the verge and barred owls calling. Free, and far quieter than the Everglades road.
